method: Original summaries checked against publisher, author, library and edition catalogue evidence. Retailer-hosted publisher copy is explicitly identified. Exact production edition identities bind the text; different editions may support work content but not edition-specific features. No private Search Console data or source excerpts are published.

entries.title: A cactus in the desert
entries.author: Teresa Wairimu Kinyanjui
entries.text: Teresa Wairimu Kinyanjui recounts her upbringing in rural Kenya and the family history that shaped her life. The autobiography follows her experience of a religious calling and the development of her preaching ministry. She describes spiritual encounters and events she understands as miracles from her own Christian perspective. The book connects those experiences with her personal journey, offering an account of faith and ministry told by the woman at its centre.
entries.identityNotes: Author ministry website describes the autobiography; exact 2011 Revival Springs Media ISBN independently confirmed in AfricaBib. Religious experiences attributed to the author.

entries.title: Child bride
entries.author: Suzanne Finstad
entries.text: Suzanne Finstad examines Priscilla Beaulieu Presley's life, from her teenage connection with Elvis Presley to marriage and a later role in the business surrounding his legacy. Drawing on interviews with Priscilla and people around the couple, Finstad investigates the relationship behind their public image. The biography follows changing personal circumstances, ambition and loss, presenting the author's interpretation of a life closely tied to one of popular music's most famous figures.
entries.identityNotes: Work synopsis corroborated by publisher; selected Arrow ISBN is the 1998 edition in Google Books. Removed wording that conflated meeting Elvis at fourteen with marriage; omitted unverified allegations. No later-edition extras claimed.

entries.title: Elsewhere
entries.author: Gabrielle Zevin
entries.text: Fifteen-year-old Liz Hall arrives in Elsewhere after her death and discovers that its inhabitants grow younger instead of older. Living with a grandmother she never knew, she struggles to accept a future that seems to reverse everything she wanted: a driving licence, graduation and adulthood. Gabrielle Zevin follows Liz as she tries to hold on to the life she lost while confronting the possibility of belonging somewhere new.
entries.identityNotes: Author synopsis supports work-level plot; selected Bloomsbury edition comes from the captured exact ISBN identity. No deluxe-edition features claimed.

entries.title: Salammbo
entries.author: Gustave Flaubert
entries.text: In ancient Carthage, unpaid mercenary soldiers turn against the city they have served. Salammbô, the daughter of the general Hamilcar, becomes caught in the conflict surrounding the soldier Matho and a stolen sacred veil. Gustave Flaubert combines a struggle for power with religious devotion and destructive desire. The novel moves between the city and the rebels as personal obsessions become entangled with the violence of war.
entries.identityNotes: Work-level plot checked against the English text, not the automatically generated catalogue summary. No translator or edition extras claimed.

entries.title: The No Asshole Rule
entries.author: Robert I. Sutton
entries.text: Robert I. Sutton examines how humiliating and hostile behaviour damages working life, then considers what employees and organisations can do about it. The book combines workplace examples with ways to recognise destructive conduct, establish standards and respond when colleagues ignore them. Sutton also turns the question back on the reader, encouraging an examination of one's own behaviour. Its focus is on making respectful treatment a practical part of everyday work.
entries.identityNotes: Publisher page is the original 2007 ebook, not the forthcoming twentieth-anniversary revision. Exact 2007 hardcover ISBN and contents corroborated by Iowa Valley library catalogue.

entries.title: Ring of Fire
entries.author: Margaret Way
entries.text: Jo is devastated when Blair, whom she has loved for years, becomes engaged to someone else. A visit to Marsh McConnell's cattle station in the Australian Outback offers a change of scene: she accompanies his young niece and nephew there. As Jo responds to the landscape and to Marsh himself, another woman's interest in him brings unexpected jealousy. Margaret Way's romance follows the uncertainty of moving beyond a lost love.
entries.identityNotes: Exact Harlequin ISBN, author, setting and characters in edition catalogue; plot corroborated by University of Birmingham Romance Wiki. Catalogue evidence, not a claim of direct access to publisher archives.

entries.title: Akira, Vol. 1
entries.author: Katsuhiro Ōtomo
entries.text: Neo-Tokyo stands where a devastating explosion once destroyed Tokyo. Teenage friends Kaneda and Tetsuo become caught in a new crisis when Tetsuo begins to develop extraordinary mental powers. A secretive agency pursues him, fearing a repetition of the earlier catastrophe and the force known as Akira. This first volume of Katsuhiro Otomo's manga introduces a city living with the aftermath of destruction and a friendship threatened by powers neither boy understands.
entries.identityNotes: Publisher distributor page matches exact Kodansha volume-one ISBN. Summary contains only opening-volume premise.

entries.title: The philanthropy of George Soros
entries.author: Chuck Sudetic
entries.text: Chuck Sudetic investigates the ideas and decisions behind George Soros's charitable work through the Open Society Foundations. The book follows projects across different countries, including support for civil society in eastern Europe and assistance during the siege of Sarajevo. It examines how the idea of an open society translates into specific interventions. With an introduction by Soros, the account concentrates on the aims and practice of his philanthropy rather than his investment career.
entries.identityNotes: Publisher describes same work in ebook format; selected hardcover ISBN is bound separately. Promotional claims and historic donation amounts omitted.

entries.title: Introduction to machine learning
entries.author: Ethem Alpaydin
entries.text: Ethem Alpaydin presents machine learning through methods drawn from statistics, pattern recognition and artificial intelligence. This second edition covers supervised learning, neural networks, hidden Markov models and reinforcement learning, with additional chapters on kernel methods, graphical models and Bayesian estimation. Explanations connect mathematical formulations to algorithms that readers can implement. The textbook assumes prior study of programming, probability, calculus and linear algebra, making it suited to advanced undergraduate and graduate coursework.
entries.identityNotes: Exact ISBN on MIT Press second-edition page. Edition-specific additions and prerequisites verified there; no fourth-edition material imported.

entries.title: BOY ERASED
entries.author: Garrard Conley
entries.text: Growing up as a Baptist pastor's son in Arkansas, Garrard Conley struggles to reconcile his sexuality with the expectations of family and church. After being outed while at college, he enters a church-supported conversion programme under pressure to change. His memoir recounts that experience and his effort to understand the people and beliefs that shaped it. Conley explores identity, shame, faith and the difficult search for self-acceptance while remaining connected to those he loves.
entries.identityNotes: Author synopsis supports memoir content. Selected UK film tie-in ISBN corroborated by Guardian Bookshop; do not infer publication date from conflicting retailer metadata.

entries.title: Koning Willem III en zijn bastaarden
entries.author: H. de Iongh
entries.text: Hanno de Iongh brengt de vermeende buitenechtelijke nakomelingen van koning Willem III en hun families in kaart. Het boek benadert de geschiedenis van het Huis van Oranje-Nassau vanuit afstamming en familieverbanden. Deze uitgave uit 2013 bouwt voort op De bastaarden van koning Gorilla en hun nakomelingen. Het gaat om een overzicht van mogelijke verwantschappen; de genoemde afstamming moet daarom niet zonder meer als bewezen worden gelezen.
entries.identityNotes: Exact ISBN and earlier-title relationship confirmed by national library catalogue. Preserves its explicit qualification that descendants are alleged; no genealogical claims presented as proven.

entries.title: The Cyberiad
entries.author: Stanisław Lem
entries.text: The constructors Trurl and Klapaucius devise extraordinary machines in a universe where engineering takes the place of fairy-tale magic. Their inventions lead to rivalries, impossible requests and consequences that escape their makers' intentions. Stanisław Lem uses these comic science-fiction tales to question what intelligence and technical power can achieve. Wordplay and fantastic inventions accompany recurring problems of ambition, cooperation and the difficulty of designing a better world.
entries.identityNotes: Author estate website includes commentary and an excerpt featuring Trurl and Klapaucius. Work-level summary only; no claims about selected edition illustrations or translator.

entries.title: Without Trust
entries.author: Penny Jordan
entries.sourceName: Open Library — Mills & Boon edition catalogue
entries.text: Accused of a crime by her cousin, Lark Cummings faces the uncompromising prosecutor James Wolfe. When the case is dropped, a job with a wealthy widow seems to offer a fresh start. Lark then discovers that James is her employer's son. Attraction now complicates her distrust of the man who treated her harshly in court. Penny Jordan's romance centres on whether Lark can risk opening her life to him again.
entries.identityNotes: Exact selected ISBN in edition catalogue; work premise corroborated by publisher-supplied ebook synopsis at Casa del Libro. Original wording, not restoration of an external description snapshot.

entries.title: Down Girl
entries.author: Kate Manne
entries.text: Kate Manne asks how misogyny operates and why it can persist even as expectations about gender change. Her account treats it as a system that disciplines women who challenge male dominance, rather than simply an individual dislike of women. She distinguishes that account from sexism and examines the different treatment of women who comply with or resist established roles. The book offers a philosophical framework for interpreting public controversies and everyday experiences.
entries.identityNotes: Exact paperback ISBN on publisher page. Describes Manne's philosophical argument as her account, not as an uncontested definition.

entries.title: Kinderen opvoeden
entries.author: Stef Desodt
entries.text: Stef Desodt vertrekt vanuit vragen die ouders en grootouders in het dagelijks leven tegenkomen. Hij bespreekt onder meer grenzen stellen, belonen en straffen, luisteren naar kinderen en omgaan met gevoelens. Ook schoolrijpheid, spelen, zakgeld en de rol van grootouders komen aan bod. Het boek presenteert praktische antwoorden vanuit de visie van de auteur en is opgebouwd rond herkenbare opvoedingssituaties. De nadruk ligt op duidelijke afspraken en aandacht voor het kind.
entries.identityNotes: Exact Lannoo ISBN in bol catalogue; supplied description corroborated in BoekenBalie listing. Publisher copy is accessed through a retailer, not a direct Lannoo page. No clinical efficacy or universal guarantees claimed.

entries.title: The Caves of Steel
entries.author: Isaac Asimov
entries.text: Detective Elijah Baley must investigate the murder of a prominent Spacer while working alongside a partner he does not trust: the humanoid robot R. Daneel Olivaw. The case unfolds against tensions between an overcrowded Earth and the societies that have settled other worlds. Isaac Asimov combines a murder investigation with questions about prejudice, technology and cooperation, as Baley has to reconsider his assumptions while searching for the killer.
entries.identityNotes: Publisher work premise confirms detective, robot partner and murder. Avoided the publisher blurb's questionable Outer Worlds journey wording and any features of the current reissue.

entries.title: Holt science & technology life science
entries.author: Holt, Rinehart and Winston, Inc.
entries.text: This life-science textbook introduces the study of living organisms through units on cells, heredity, evolution and classification. It then examines plants and other organisms, animals, ecology, the systems of the human body and human health. The sequence moves from basic biological structures to relationships among organisms and their environments. The 2001 Holt edition brings these subjects together as a structured course, with an index for finding topics throughout the book.
entries.identityNotes: Internet Archive edition catalogue lists the eight textbook units and 2001 publisher. Exact ISBN corroborated in Open Library record. No promise that a used copy includes a LabBook, teacher materials or access codes.

entries.title: Exodus
entries.author: Paul Collier
entries.sourceName: Oxford University Press — Google Books catalogue
entries.text: Paul Collier examines migration from the perspectives of people who move, the communities they leave and the societies that receive them. He considers how economic and social effects vary with the scale of migration, and asks what that means for policy. Drawing on research and examples, the book sets out Collier's argument for rethinking migration rules. It invites readers to consider competing interests rather than treating migration as a question with a single, uniform outcome.
entries.identityNotes: Exact OUP ISBN and contents in Google Books, supplemented by publisher author discussion. Corrects provider typo and attributes policy judgments to Collier.

entries.title: Spark
entries.author: John J. Ratey
entries.text: John J. Ratey, writing with Eric Hagerman, explores research on physical activity and the brain. He discusses connections with learning, attention, mood and stress, using case studies that include a school fitness programme in Naperville, Illinois. The book presents Ratey's argument for giving exercise a more prominent place in everyday life. Its focus is on the relationship between movement and mental functioning, and the examples through which the author explains that relationship.
entries.identityNotes: Exact hardcover ISBN and coauthor on publisher page. Replaces sweeping treatment and prevention claims with a neutral description of the book's subject and argument.
